about: Stages and timing for the lapsed-customers playbook. scripts/handoff.py reads this file: the stages it tracks, the outcomes each stage can record, and how long to wait between stages. Each key is explained under notes.

stages.name: size
stages.do: Size lapsing and lapsed customers by recency, frequency and value, add the uncovered groups as findings, and ask the user which one to win back.

stages.name: refine
stages.do: Test the lapsing patterns (high-value customers slowing down, one-time buyers past their repeat window, new customers with no second order, category affinity matched to trending searches) for a sharper audience than the recency group.

skip_when.reason: the size stage found no uncovered lapsed group worth winning back.

stages.name: segment
stages.do: Define and size the chosen audience, reuse a segment that already matches, or create one after its own yes.

skip_when.reason: the size stage found no uncovered lapsed group worth winning back.

stages.name: launch
stages.do: Clone a proven win-back scenario as a draft after its own yes, or find there is nothing to clone.

skip_when.reason: the size stage found no uncovered lapsed group worth winning back.
there is no audience for the flow.

stages.name: adapt
stages.do: Point the draft's audience condition at the new segment and make the fix list's step changes, or build the flow from the outline, each after its own yes.

skip_when.reason: the size stage found no uncovered lapsed group worth winning back.
there is no audience for the flow.
the user stopped before any flow was made.

stages.name: test
stages.do: Optionally add an A/B split to the draft (a message, holdout or timing test) after its own yes, before QA so QA sees the split; record no_test, or skip the stage, when the user doesn't want a test.

skip_when.reason: the size stage found no uncovered lapsed group worth winning back.
there is no audience for the flow.
the user stopped before any flow was made.
no flow was built.

stages.name: qa
stages.do: QA the draft, with its A/B split if the test stage added one, until it is GO; a NO-GO fix goes back through the adapt stage's write skill (engagement-scenario-builder), with its own yes, and is QA'd again. Then wait for the user to switch it on in the Engagement UI, record the day it started, and record the switch-on as a change (source engagement-ui).

skip_when.reason: the size stage found no uncovered lapsed group worth winning back.
there is no audience for the flow.
the user stopped before any flow was made.
no flow was built.

stages.name: ab-read-out
stages.do: Read out the test stage's split on its agreed primary metric: call the winner, keep it running until a later date, or stop as inconclusive. The user acts on the verdict in the Engagement UI.

skip_when.reason: the size stage found no uncovered lapsed group worth winning back.
there is no audience for the flow.
the user stopped before any flow was made.
no flow was built.
the flow was never switched on.
no A/B split was added, so there is no test to read out.
the test stage was skipped, so there is no test to read out.

stages.name: performance
stages.do: Read the flow's results step by step since it started: sends, clicks, unsubscribes and recipients who bought soon after.

stages.name: impact
stages.do: Measure reactivation (purchases by the lapsed audience) before and after the flow started, against a control, for a revenue verdict with a range.

notes.measure_after_days: Days after the qa stage finishes (the day the user switched the flow on) before the performance and impact stages are due. A win-back sequence usually spreads its messages over several weeks, so six weeks lets most of the first entrants finish it; change-impact-tracker needs about 14 days after a change for a verdict other than too early to tell.
notes.readout_after_days: Days after the flow started (the qa stage's done date) before the ab-read-out stage is due. engagement-ab-test-setup sizes a test in whole weeks and never below its min_test_days, which engagement-experiment-readout uses too; 14 matches that minimum. When the test stage agreed a later end date, the readout says keep running: record keep_running with that date.
notes.wait_outcomes: Outcomes that mean a stage isn't finished yet. The script records them only with status in_progress and a --not-before date to come back on, so status never shows the stage as due before then. keep_running is the ab-read-out stage's wait, when the test needs more customers or days; inconclusive is its way out when the test never reaches its sample.
notes.playbooks: Each playbook's title, product and stages in order. A stage names the skill that does it, whether that skill writes, what to do, the outcomes it can record, not_before (wait this rules key's number of days after another stage is done) and skip_when (suggest skipping when another stage had one of these outcomes; skips don't cascade, so each stage lists every earlier outcome that ends the run). Two stages are not in the original proposal: adapt, because scenario-template-launcher clones a source as it is and never edits it, so pointing the clone at the new segment is engagement-scenario-builder's job; and impact, because engagement-scenario-performance counts buyers, not revenue, so change-impact-tracker measures the whole flow before and after, against a control. segment-opportunity-finder can use Bloomreach Discovery search trends itself (its pattern P5); the run's context stays Engagement only. The test stage is optional: engagement-ab-test-setup adds an A/B split (a message, holdout or timing test) to the draft before the qa stage, so scenario-qa checks the split too, and records its write from its plan and verify files. When the user doesn't want a test, they skip the stage (or it records no_test), and status then offers ab-read-out as a skip. ab-read-out (engagement-experiment-readout) reads the split out before the performance and impact stages, so the controlled answer comes first.
